diagnosis: Assessment of clonality with antibody to TRBC1 (JOVI-1)
legend: Only T cells (CD3-positive) are shown. A–C FNAB from reactive lymph node. A 78% of T cells are CD4+ (orange and purple) and 19% are CD8+ (green). B Only CD4+ T cells are shown; 4% of T cells are CD4+ CD10+ (purple) and 74% are CD4+ CD10− (orange). C 56% of CD4+ CD10+ cells, 54% of CD4+ CD10− cells, and 48% of CD8+ cells are positive for TRBC1. Therefore, TRBC1 did not detect a monoclonal population. D–F Bone marrow aspirate from a known T-cell lymphoma case. D 75% of T cells are CD4+ and 21% are CD8+ (green). E Only CD4+ T cells are shown; 62% of T cells are CD4+ CD7− (purple) and 13% are CD4+ CD7+ (orange). F 99% of CD4+ CD7− cells, 53% of CD4+ CD7+ cells, and 24% of CD8+ cells are positive for TRBC1. Therefore, the CD4+ CD7− cells are essentially uniformly positive for TRBC1, indicating a monoclonal population.

diagnosis: B cell population with abnormal scatter properties
legend: A Normal lymphocytes (purple) have low forward and side scatter. Other cells (red) have higher forward and side scatter. B The cells coloured red are shown to be B cells by staining with CD19 and CD20.

diagnosis: Flow cytometry of an FNAB of a normal lymph node
legend: Each plot displays more than 8000 lymphocytes. B cells are shown in blue, T cells in red, and granulocytes (Panel A only) in green. A All cells. CD45 versus side scatter (SSC) shows a large lymphocyte population (red T cells and blue B cells). The granulocyte population (green) is small (4% of cells), indicating little blood contamination. B–F Lymphocytes only. B 97% of lymphocytes are either T cells (CD3+) or B cells (CD19+ and/or CD20+). C The B cells are uniformly positive for both CD19 and CD20. D Assessment of surface light chains shows that the B cells are polyclonal, with a mixture of kappa+ and lambda+ cells and a kappa:lambda ratio of 1.8:1. E Nearly all the B cells are negative for CD5. F Nearly all the B cells are negative for CD10.

diagnosis: Flow cytometric features of mast cells, in a lymph node FNAB in a patient with mast cell sarcoma
legend: A The mast cells (purple) lie within the granulocyte gate in the side scatter versus CD45 plot. B The CD117 on the mast cells is very bright, brighter than the CD117 on the normal myeloid blasts (magenta).

diagnosis: Flow cytometry of myeloid sarcoma in a lymph node FNAB
legend: A 75% of events are in the blast gate (magenta). B,C The blasts are positive for CD33 and CD117, and negative for all T-cell and B-cell markers (not shown). The blasts were not detected in the bone marrow.

diagnosis: Small monoclonal B-cell population with a background of polyclonal B cells
legend: A All lymphocytes are shown. The bright CD19-positive and CD20-positive population is shown in green. B–D B cells only. B The B cells with normal light chain intensity are shown in red (kappa-positive) and blue (lambda-positive). The green population is restricted to lambda, and its lambda staining is dim. The green population is largely negative for CD10 (C) and CD5 (D). Thus the small monoclonal population is dim lambda+ CD5− CD10− CD19++ and CD20++.

diagnosis: Determination of B-cell monoclonality by multiparametric flow cytometry
legend: Kappa/lambda/CD19/CD20/CD5/CD10. <strong>A</strong> Identification of B cells by CD19 and side scatter (SSC) gating. <strong>B</strong> Doublet exclusion by forward scatter (FSC) area versus width gating. <strong>C</strong> Cell size discrimination by FSC and SSC gating. <strong>D</strong> The small cells (in light blue) include kappa-positive and lambda-positive cells. <strong>E</strong> The large cells (in dark blue) are lambda-restricted. <strong>F</strong> The CD10-positive and CD10-negative subsets are marked red and light blue, respectively. <strong>G</strong> The CD10-positive cells are brighter for CD20 than the CD10-negative cells. <strong>H</strong> The CD10-positive cells are monoclonal, lambda-restricted. <strong>I</strong> The CD10-negative cells are polyclonal.

title: Pitfalls in flow cytometry of cytopathology samples; this table focusses on interpretation of flow cytometry data – it does not cover pitfalls in sample preparation and performance of flow cytometry, which are reviewed elsewhere {31697047}
source: The Table is based on text drafted by William Robert Geddie.
tablehtml:
Cell type

Pitfalls

Comments

Actions

Any

Declaring normal variations to be lymphoma

Examples:

·   Dim CD5+ CD8+ T cells

·   CD7− CD4+ T cells

·   CD10+ bright CD20+ dim polyclonal light chain–positive B cells (reactive follicular hyperplasia)

Familiarity with normal variations in lymphocyte phenotype {31697047; 30194715}

 

Gating excludes CD45-negative haematopoietic cells

Some cases of plasma cell neoplasm and B-cell LBL are CD45-negative

Check all events (open gate) for relevant markers, e.g. bright CD38 for plasma cells and CD19 for B-cell LBL

Large

Gating excludes large lymphoid cells

The lymphocyte gate may miss lymphomas with abnormal CD45, forward scatter, or side scatter properties; such lymphomas may be falsely considered to be neutrophils or monocytes {30729667; 30549186}

Check all events (open gate) for key lymphocyte markers

 

Failure to consider that large cells might be myeloid sarcoma

Myeloid sarcoma is typically CD45+ and low-moderate side scatter (in the “blast gate”) {28574302}

Check populations in the blast gate for myeloid markers

 

Failure to consider that large cells might be non-haematopoietic tumours

Non-haematopoietic tumours detected by flow cytometry are typically CD45−; the commonest are small cell lung carcinoma and other tumours of neuroendocrine origin; common leukocyte markers expressed by such tumours include CD56, CD117, CD138, and CD10 {31587038; 10705818}

Consider whether CD45− populations with atypical markers are non-haematopoietic tumours

 

Hodgkin lymphoma

Detection of CHL cells has been reported with special techniques {34293084; 30350336}, but in many laboratories this is often not feasible {21438908; 32343479}; detection of NLPHL by flow cytometry is also controversial {30350336; 32343479}

Use cell block for immunohistochemical staining when Hodgkin lymphoma is a possibility

Small-intermediate

Detection of small clonal B-cell population

B-cell populations, apparently clonal by light chain expression, often CD10+, often in children or young adults, may be detected, but they lack histopathological evidence of malignancy and clinical progression {15080297; 23042004}

Inclusion of comment in report that detection of a clonal population is not diagnostic of malignancy, especially in children and young adults, or in the setting of autoimmune disease {16482990}

 

Misclassification

Some lymphomas have aberrant antigen expression patterns, such as CD10-positive mantle cell lymphoma {26124315}

Familiarity with variations in lymphoma phenotype

 

Dual surface immunoglobulin light chain expression

Lymphoma cells appear to express both kappa and lambda light chains

Attempt to resolve this by using alternative pairs of antibodies for surface light chains {22095382}

Not applicable

Peripheral blood contamination

The presence of a substantial granulocyte population is a clue {31697047}; blood contamination reduces capacity to detect abnormal populations in FNAB material

Include comment in report

CHL, classic Hodgkin lymphoma; LBL, lymphoblastic lymphoma; NLPHL, nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma.
